density-curve.def: A density curve is a smooth curve that models a distribution: it is on or above the horizontal axis and has an area of exactly 1 under it. The area under the curve over an interval is the proportion of values, or the probability, in that interval.

normal-distribution.def: A normal distribution, written $N(\mu, \sigma)$, has a symmetric, bell-shaped density curve centered at its mean $\mu$, with standard deviation $\sigma$ setting its spread. It models many roughly symmetric, mound-shaped distributions.

standard-normal.def: The standard normal distribution is the normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 1, $N(0, 1)$. Standardizing a value, $z = \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$, turns any normal question into a standard normal one, answered by Table A or technology.

empirical-rule.def: The empirical rule (68-95-99.7 rule): in a normal distribution about 68% of values lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean, about 95% within 2, and about 99.7% within 3.
